title: Impact of Deferring Public Transport Fare Increments
what_it_is: Impact of Deferring Public Transport Fare Increments

sections.label: Fare increase and concession passes
sections.summary: Questions ask whether the deferred 15.6% fare increase will be expunged and about public transport spending and hybrid concession passes for PwDs and seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Public Transport Council plans to expunge the 15.6% fare increase deferred for future Fare Review Exercises (FREs) after a 7% increase having been granted in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the mean and median monthly spend on public transport in the past 12 months by (i) persons with disabilities (PwDs) and (ii) seniors who use public transport; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider introducing hybrid monthly concession passes for PwDs and seniors to be made available in different denominations for light, moderate and heavy users.

sections.label: Fare formula output drivers
sections.summary: The fare formula output was 12%, driven by a 62% energy price increase, about 7% wage growth and about 4% core inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In this year's FRE, the fare formula output was 12%, driven by a 62% increase in energy prices, strong national wage growth at about 7%, and core inflation at about 4%.

sections.label: PTC fare increase and subsidies
sections.summary: PTC decided on a 7% fare increase, less than a third of the 22.6% maximum, with $300 million additional Government subsidies in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Instead, the PTC decided on an overall fare increase of 7% – which is less than a third of the maximum allowable fare increase of 22.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To account for this funding gap, the Government will provide $300 million of additional subsidies in 2023, which is $100 million more than the previous year.

sections.label: Rail operators' financial results
sections.summary: After Government grants, SBS Transit rail operations lost several million dollars while SMRT Trains had a $6 million operating profit, under 1% margin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In the latest financial year, after accounting for Government grants, SBS Transit reported a loss of several million dollars for their rail operations, while SMRT Corporation (SMRT) Trains reported an operating profit of $6 million, which represents a profit margin of less than 1%.

sections.label: Hybrid pass price reduction
sections.summary: Hybrid monthly concession pass prices will be reduced by up to 10% and a new discounted WTCS monthly pass introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As heavy users of public transport will be more affected by the increase in per-journey fares, we will reduce the price of hybrid monthly concession passes by up to 10%, and introduce a new discounted WTCS monthly pass.

sections.label: PTV amount increase
sections.summary: The Government will increase the PTV amount from $30 in 2022 to $50 this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government will increase the PTV amount from $30 in 2022 to $50 this year.

sections.label: Public transport reliability standards
sections.summary: Public transport operators face stringent service standards that have not been relaxed, and since 2019 MKBF has exceeded one million train kilometres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: On reliability, the public transport operators are subject to stringent service standards and we have not relaxed these standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Since 2019, MKBF has exceeded one million train kilometres.

sections.label: SMRT kaizen savings
sections.summary: SMRT shared that in the latest year, kaizen allowed them to save more than $100 million in total.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: When I visited SMRT, they shared with me that in the latest year, "kaizen" has allowed them to save more than $100 million, in total.

sections.label: Fare increase and government subsidy
sections.summary: The maximum fare adjustment was 22.6% but PTC approved a 7% increase, with the Government providing $300 million in subsidies for the deferred gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This year, for example, the maximum amount that could be set was 22.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But the PTC did exactly like what Mr Chua mentioned, they factored in all these different considerations and they decided that we should only increase by less than a third, 7%, and the rest will be deferred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But when we say "deferred", what it actually means is that the Government is then topping up to ensure that this funding gap is provided for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And in this year's fare review, the Government is providing $300 million of subsidies to cater to this gap.

sections.label: Bus contracting tender competition
sections.summary: Bus service fees are based on bids, and with four bus operators and refined contracting, service fees and margins have come down in recent contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And they bid and then, the service fee, based on the bids, that is what we pay them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I would be happy to share with the House that over time, as we do more bus contracting tenders and as of now, there are more operators – there are now four bus operators – the bids are also becoming more competitive and we have also refined the way we do the bus contracting, that the service fees and the margins have been coming down in the more recent contracts.

sections.label: Additional subsidy for fare deferment
sections.summary: An additional $300 million subsidy will cover the fare deferment and help cushion the fare increase for commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For the coming year, there will be an additional $300 million subsidy to cover the fare deferment, which I have explained earlier, and these subsidies go towards helping commuters, because they help to cushion the fare increase that is needed.

sections.label: PTC to consider flexibility options
sections.summary: The PTC will be asked to consider different options on whether more flexibility can be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We can take a look to see how we can do this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will ask the PTC to consider different options, whether there are ways in which we can provide more flexibility.

sections.label: PTV quantum rationale
sections.summary: The question asks for the rationale for setting the PTV quantum at $50 and whether it can be increased further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given this, what is the rationale for setting the PTV quantum at $50 and can this be increased further?

sections.label: PTV purpose and coverage
sections.summary: PTVs are meant to cushion the fare increase impact on lower-income households, not defray total public transport expenditure, and $50 covers about six months of fare increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The PTVs are not designed or not intended to defray the total public transport expenditure, but rather, they are meant to cushion the impact of the fare increase on lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, if you look at it from that point of view, we estimate that $50 would cover about six months of fare increase for these households.

sections.label: Start date for this round
sections.summary: For this round, they can start doing so from early-2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For this round, they can start doing so from early-2024.
